subject: Plan adjustment & credit structure — Acme Analytics proposal
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Plan adjustment & credit structure — Acme Analytics proposal

Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion I attached an updated pricing_grid_acme_v2.xlsx that maps your current usage to three simple choices: keep current committed tier with a one-time upgrade credit, move to a flexible monthly plan with higher per-token price but no commitment, or a hybrid commit + burst option.

Two specific items I wanted to call out:
- Upgrade credit: we can apply a one-time credit equal to the remaining committed months pro-rated up to 20% of the current annual commit if you decide to upgrade to the next tier before your renewal.
- Downgrade path: downgrades during a committed term are allowed but incur a 90-day notice and the remainder of the commit is billed; we can structure a partial credit applied to future Dedicated capacity purchases instead.

Attached: pricing_grid_acme_v2.xlsx (breakdown) and a draft SOW outline (proposed_mop_sow.pdf).

Questions for you:
1) Which of the three options do you want priced as a formal quote?
2) Would your procurement team prefer the credit as a refundable invoice credit or a discount applied up front?

I'll loop Ben (sales ops) if we need to engineer the credit flows.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
+1 415-555-0123

Attachments: pricing_grid_acme_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), proposed_mop_sow.pdf (PDF)

From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T18:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Plan adjustment & credit structure — Acme Analytics proposal

Monica —

Appreciate the clear options. A couple quick clarifying items from procurement:
- If we upgrade mid-term, can the one-time credit be used against services (e.g., migration support) as well as billing credits? Our legal prefers credits to be tied to services vs open invoice credits.
- For downgrades: our forecast shows a potential dip in Q4. If we give notice today for a Q4 downgrade, do we still get pro-rated credit back to our account or is it only applied to future purchases?

Also, can you provide an example amortization schedule showing how a 12-month commit + 3-month mid-term upgrade would look numerically? That will help the FP&A team.

Cc'ing Aisha from procurement (aisha.procure@acmeanalytics.com) who will own the PO side.

Thanks,
Tom
Head of Engineering | Acme Analytics

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acmeanalytics.com>, Aisha Procurement <aisha.procure@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Plan adjustment & credit structure — Acme Analytics proposal

Tom/Aisha —

Short answers up front: yes, credit can be scoped to be used for services (migration/onboarding/retainer work) OR as an invoice credit — we can reflect whichever you prefer on the quote. For downgrades, the default is the 90-day notice + remainder billed, but we can offer a partial conversion of the unused commit into a platform credit valid for 12 months to be used on future Dedicated purchases or professional services.

Ben is looping in the example amortization schedule and a small worked example that shows: current commit, mid-term upgrade applied month X, one-time credit applied against professional services, and resulting cash flows.

Proposed next step: Ben will attach the amortization and two formal quote variants (credit-as-service vs credit-as-invoice) so procurement can pick. If Aisha prefers, we can produce a single consolidated quote with the credit line-item and a separate SOW for services.

Thanks —
Monica

Hi all —

Attached is the amortization example and two quote variants (see pricing_grid_acme_v2.xlsx updated tab "Worked Examples"). Summary:
- Scenario A (upgrade now to Tier C): one-time credit = min(20% of annual commit, remaining pro-rated months * monthly rate). In your case that's $45k credit if applied to services, or $40k as invoice credit (tax treatment noted on the quote).
- Scenario B (flex monthly): no credit; higher unit price but no term penalty.
- Downgrade handling: if notice given with >90 days, unused months are converted to platform credit at 60% of nominal value (this is the concession we agreed for strategic accounts).

If procurement wants the credit applied to services, I recommend itemizing the services SOW and putting the credit as a line item in DocuSign so legal sees the restriction. DocuSign powerform link below for the quote.

DocuSign (quote + SOW): https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abcd-1234
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567

If you confirm Scenario A, I'll produce final quote & SOW for signatures today.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Sales Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
